title: Preemption-aware CUDA-Graph Segmentation and Kernel Affinity for Mixed Prefill/Decode Streams
creator: Lena Cho
description:
Background: Our current CUDA-graph capture and replay strategy yields intermittent incorrectness and failovers for mixed workloads that interleave long prefill batches with low-latency decode streams. Root causes we have observed include: (1) graph captures that assume contiguous kernel binding across an entire prefill window which becomes invalid under mid-capture preemption, (2) kernel selection that does not account for concurrent stream priorities and hardware affinity, and (3) KV-cache and attention state not consistently checkpointed when a graph is segmented for stability.

Goal: Implement a preemption-aware graph segmentation strategy plus a lightweight kernel-affinity heuristic that (a) keeps capture windows sufficiently small to limit re-capture cost under preemption, (b) binds high-priority decode kernels to preferred SM/stream affinities to reduce tail latency, and (c) checkpoints ephemeral KV/attention state at segment boundaries to guarantee replay correctness without full-prefill reruns. This should reduce capture-related errors by >90% for mixed workloads and reduce median tail-latency regressions for P99-sensitive applications.
acceptance_criteria: Capture stability: Segmented captures reduce user-visible capture failures in our mixed-prefill workload benchmark from current baseline to <5% of runs.
Correctness: Replay of segmented captures reproduces identical token outputs (byte-identical) for 99.9% of deterministic tests; remaining diffs must be documented and explained.
Latency: High-priority decode latency (P99) improves or remains neutral compared to current stable branch under mixed load at 80% capacity.
Cost: Re-capture overhead (extra GPU work) remains below 12% additional cost for typical prefill sizes in our internal workloads.
Rollout: Feature gated and gradual rollout with canary at runtime-1.19; rollback path validated.
Monitoring: Dashboard graphs for capture failures, re-capture rate, KV-checkpoint size, and kernel-affinity misbinds present and alerting thresholds set.
technical_notes: Segmentation model: divide prefill capture into adaptive segments sized by effective token entropy and expected preemption probability. Use historical host preemption metrics to pick segment length; floor at 64 tokens and cap at 2048 tokens.

Kernel affinity heuristic: runtime observes active stream mix; label kernels as 'latency-sensitive' (decode) or 'throughput' (prefill) and prefer assigning latency-sensitive kernels to streams with lower queue depth and SM locality where supported by driver.

Ephemeral KV checkpointing: at segment boundaries, persist minimal KV snapshot (pointer + checksum + small delta) into an in-memory and optionally host-mapped staging buffer to support fast merge during replay. Checkpoints are versioned and tombstoned after successful full decode.

Consistency model: implement deterministic merge logic for checkpointed KV state so that segmented replay composes identical KV state to a monolithic prefill when no external nondeterminism occurs. For nondeterministic cases (e.g., cudaGraph fallback), emit a divergence event and route request to safe fallback (serial prefill).

Capture policy: when a prefill is interrupted mid-capture by a higher-priority decode, trigger immediate lightweight checkpoint and mark segment as preempted. The scheduler will attempt a local replay of remaining prefill segments instead of a full re-capture when feasible.

Fallbacks: three-tier fallback chain: (1) segmented replay merge, (2) local serial prefill on same GPU without graph replay, (3) schedule to next available GPU pool with same model variant. Rollbacks are automatic if output deviation is detected.

Instrumentation: emit trace spans for capture:start, capture:segment:create, capture:preempt, checkpoint:write, replay:merge, and kernel-affinity:assign. Add counters and histograms for re-capture latency, checkpoint sizes, and affinity hit-rate.
Safety: maintain a max checkpoint buffer budget per GPU instance to avoid OOM and fallback to full re-capture when budget exceeded.
test_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint serialization/deserialization and merge determinism across model sizes (7B, 13B, 70B).

Integration tests: synthetic mixed workload that alternates long prefill (avg 1500 tokens) with bursty decode requests; assert byte-identical outputs across 1000 trials on stable branch vs feature branch.
Fuzz harness: inject artificial preemption at different offsets during capture to exercise segment boundary behavior and ensure no kernel state leak between streams.
Performance bench: run 72-hour soak with realistic request distribution at 0.7 capacity and measure capture failure rate, average re-capture overhead, and P50/P95/P99 latency for decode streams.
Chaos experiments: simulate GPU eviction and driver retries on canary pool to validate graceful fallback chain and automated rollbacks.
CI gating: require green unit/integration/fuzz tests and no regression in the runtime perf benchmark suite (within 3% latency) before merging.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'segmented_graphs_v2' runtime flag. Default off in staging.
Phase 1 (canary): Enable for 5% of hosted traffic on a dedicated canary pool with extra logging and retention (7 days).
Phase 2 (expanded canary): 25% traffic, monitor alerts and error rates for 48h. Run chaos tests in parallel.
Phase 3 (gradual): 50% then 100% over 2 weeks if metrics stable and no correctness divergences.
Rollback: flip flag off; safe-mode path routes to serial prefill; automated revert PR ready.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Lena Cho: Spike complete. Measured baseline re-capture rate of 18% on mixed workload with 1500-token prefills. Kernel-affinity experiments show up to 22% P99 improvements when decode kernels pinned correctly.

2026-03-04 - Ethan Morales: Implemented initial segmented checkpoint format (delta + checksum). Wrote unit tests for serialization. Observed one nondeterministic merge on a 70B test (investigating floating point op order).
2026-03-06 - Priya Desai (PM): Confirmed customer ticket INF-3912 would benefit from lower P99 tail; requested prioritization. Marked customer_impact high.

2026-03-09 - Engineering review: Suggested adding max-checkpoint-budget guard and a lightweight strong-consistency flag for enterprise customers. Deferred expensive disk-backed checkpoints to later RFC.
2026-03-12 - Ethan Morales: Canary pool config ready. Added trace spans to debug headers. Preparing PR for segmentation scheduler and affinity heuristic. Next: integration bench and chaos test runs.
